paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minFDE₂₀ (in units of distance, likely meters) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at intervals of 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8). The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←)”, also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.21 to 0.24, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at a value of approximately 0.242 at 0 examples and decreasing to approximately 0.209 at 4 examples before rising to approximately 0.211 at 8 examples. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with square markers and a solid line, starting at approximately 0.231 at 0 examples and remaining relatively stable, fluctuating between approximately 0.220 and 0.224 across the range of 8 examples.
model_annotations.German: The line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES (blue line with circle markers) and Random (orange line with circle markers)—as a function of the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8, with tick marks at integer intervals. The vertical axis represents the minimum FDE20 (minFDE20), scaled linearly from 0.21 to 0.24, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is also linearly scaled. The ST-ES line begins at 0.24 at 0 examples, decreases sharply to 0.210 at 2 examples, and then fluctuates slightly between 0.210 and 0.212 through 8 examples. The Random line begins at 0.230 at 0 examples, fluctuates around 0.220 with minor variations, and ends at approximately 0.225 at 8 examples.
